readme:
# RotNet 四方向旋转预测


## 1. 问题


实现 `rotation_batch(images)` 与 `rotation_loss(logits, labels)`。RotNet 预测图像被旋转了哪一个角度，监督标签完全由施加的变换产生。本题同时练习精确图像几何和真实旋转分类训练。


## 2. 核心公式


角度为逆时针 $90r$ 度，$r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$：
$$\widetilde x_{rB+b}=R_{90r}(x_b),\quad y_{rB+b}=r,$$
$$L=\frac1M\sum_i[\operatorname{logsumexp}_{k=0}^3(s_{ik})-s_{i,y_i}].$$
输出依次为四个旋转角度的大块。`[[1,2],[3,4]]` 逆时针旋转 90° 后是 `[[2,4],[1,3]]`；均匀 logits 得到 `log(4)`。


## 3. 公式到代码


在两个空间维度上组合转置与翻转，依次拼接 0°、90°、180°、270° 视图，每种标签重复 B 次。旋转是像素置换，不能断开图像梯度。损失提取每行给定标签的分数，从稳定 log-sum-exp 中减去，再对样本求均值。


## 4. 本题约定


图像为非空、有限 float32/float64 `[B,C,H,H]`；使用正方形使四个视图尺寸一致。输出为 `[4B,C,H,H]` 与同 device 的 int64 `[4B]` 标签。按角度分块是本题批次约定，官方加载器先逐图像生成视图。无插值、裁剪、颜色变化或原地修改；支持非连续输入。损失接收任意非空 `[M,4]` logits 与范围 `[0,3]` 的 int64 `[M]` 标签，不要求 M 是 4 的倍数。1×1 图像也生成四种标签，尽管视图无法区分。


## 5. 交互图与 CPU 实验


八张确定性非对称 4×4 图案产生 32 个视图。零初始化的 16×4 线性分类头，以 `.6` 学习率做 80 次全批 SGD，实际使用两个待实现函数。T3 要求旋转准确率 1，损失低于 `.06` 且低于初始值的 5%。对称图像可能无法判断方向，因此教学图案特意选择非对称形状。旋转训练准确率不能直接证明下游表示质量。


## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸与来源


论文通过分类、检测和分割研究旋转任务的迁移效果，那需要训练图像编码器和独立下游数据。更早的预任务包括空间上下文预测与拼图。本题与已有 VQ “Rotation Trick” 无关，后者处理梯度估计，不是图像旋转自监督。


[Unsupervised Representation Learning by Predicting Image Rotations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07728) · [Official implementation](https://github.com/gidariss/FeatureLearningRotNet/blob/master/dataloader.py)

# 实现提示

建议先独立完成练习，再查看本页。

在两个空间维度上组合转置与翻转，依次拼接 0°、90°、180°、270° 视图，每种标签重复 B 次。旋转是像素置换，不能断开图像梯度。损失提取每行给定标签的分数，从稳定 log-sum-exp 中减去，再对样本求均值。

图像为非空、有限 float32/float64 `[B,C,H,H]`；使用正方形使四个视图尺寸一致。输出为 `[4B,C,H,H]` 与同 device 的 int64 `[4B]` 标签。按角度分块是本题批次约定，官方加载器先逐图像生成视图。无插值、裁剪、颜色变化或原地修改；支持非连续输入。损失接收任意非空 `[M,4]` logits 与范围 `[0,3]` 的 int64 `[M]` 标签，不要求 M 是 4 的倍数。1×1 图像也生成四种标签，尽管视图无法区分。

## 小实验与阈值

八张确定性非对称 4×4 图案产生 32 个视图。零初始化的 16×4 线性分类头，以 `.6` 学习率做 80 次全批 SGD，实际使用两个待实现函数。T3 要求旋转准确率 1，损失低于 `.06` 且低于初始值的 5%。对称图像可能无法判断方向，因此教学图案特意选择非对称形状。旋转训练准确率不能直接证明下游表示质量。

数据和初始化均为确定性；测试 fixture 还将 Python、NumPy、PyTorch 的种子设为 42。原生标定环境为 Apple silicon 上仓库固定的 PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU。NumPy 自动微分适配器与导出的 WASM 包运行同一套完整训练测试。断言证明本合成任务上的数值和学习行为，不代表论文基准复现。

## 错误实现检查

以下每个 mutant 仅隔离一种错误，完整说明对应题面约定：

- 把 90° 逆时针视图换成顺时针。
- 角度分块视图搭配逐图像循环的错误标签。
- 180° 视图未旋转。
- 切断视图到输入图像的梯度。
- 对分类损失求和而非求均值。
- 直接指数化原始 logits 导致溢出。

来源：[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07728) 与 [官方代码](https://github.com/gidariss/FeatureLearningRotNet/blob/master/dataloader.py)。

原生参考解实测：initial_loss=1.38629; final_loss=0.0371615; initial_accuracy=0.25; final_accuracy=1。

旋转只作用于空间维，必须保留所有样本和通道，即使批次、通道、空间轴都是非连续视图。标量坐标 oracle 同时检查各视图与父存储梯度。

en.title: RotNet: Predicting Four Image Rotations
en.readme:
# RotNet: Predicting Four Image Rotations


## 1. Problem


Implement `rotation_batch(images)` and `rotation_loss(logits, labels)`. RotNet learns by predicting which of four image rotations was applied. Transformation choices supply the labels automatically. This exercise preserves the exact image geometry and trains a small rotation classifier.


## 2. Core equations


For counterclockwise rotations $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ with angles $90r$ degrees,
$$\widetilde x_{rB+b}=R_{90r}(x_b),\quad y_{rB+b}=r,$$
$$L=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M[\operatorname{logsumexp}_{k=0}^3(s_{ik})-s_{i,y_i}].$$
Views are in four rotation-major blocks. A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation maps `[[1,2],[3,4]]` to `[[2,4],[1,3]]`. Equal logits yield `log(4)`.


## 3. Equations to code


Use transpose and flips on the two spatial axes, concatenate the 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° blocks, and repeat each label B times. Preserve the image autograd path: rotation is a pixel permutation. For the loss, gather the supplied class column, subtract it from stable row log-sum-exp, and average examples.


## 4. Exercise conventions


Images are nonempty finite float32/float64 `[B,C,H,H]`; square shapes allow all views to share a tensor. Output is `[4B,C,H,H]` plus int64 `[4B]` labels on the same device. Rotation-major batching is this exercise’s convention; the official data loader first creates views per sample. There is no interpolation, crop, color transform or input mutation. Loss accepts any nonempty `[M,4]` logits and int64 `[M]` labels in `[0,3]`, even when M is not a multiple of four. Strided images work. A 1×1 image still gets all four labels although those views are indistinguishable.


## 5. Interactive plots and CPU lab


Eight deterministic asymmetric 4×4 glyphs generate 32 rotated examples. A zero-initialized 16×4 linear head learns for 80 full-batch SGD updates at learning rate `.6`. Both submitted functions are used. T3 requires rotation accuracy 1 and loss below `.06` and 5% of its initial value. Symmetric images cannot always reveal their rotation; the synthetic glyphs are chosen to make this pretext task learnable. Rotation accuracy alone is not evidence of transfer representation quality.


## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Extensions and sources


The paper studies transfer from rotation prediction to classification, detection and segmentation. Those evaluations require a trained image encoder and separate downstream data. Related early pretext tasks predict spatial context or solve jigsaws. This module is distinct from the existing VQ “Rotation Trick” exercise, which concerns a gradient estimator rather than image-rotation supervision.


[Unsupervised Representation Learning by Predicting Image Rotations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07728) · [Official implementation](https://github.com/gidariss/FeatureLearningRotNet/blob/master/dataloader.py)
en.notes:
# Implementation notes

Read these after attempting the exercise.

Use transpose and flips on the two spatial axes, concatenate the 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° blocks, and repeat each label B times. Preserve the image autograd path: rotation is a pixel permutation. For the loss, gather the supplied class column, subtract it from stable row log-sum-exp, and average examples.

Images are nonempty finite float32/float64 `[B,C,H,H]`; square shapes allow all views to share a tensor. Output is `[4B,C,H,H]` plus int64 `[4B]` labels on the same device. Rotation-major batching is this exercise’s convention; the official data loader first creates views per sample. There is no interpolation, crop, color transform or input mutation. Loss accepts any nonempty `[M,4]` logits and int64 `[M]` labels in `[0,3]`, even when M is not a multiple of four. Strided images work. A 1×1 image still gets all four labels although those views are indistinguishable.

The maintained mutations isolate these faults:

- Swap clockwise/counterclockwise 90-degree views.
- Use sample-major labels for rotation-major views.
- Leave the 180-degree view unrotated.
- Detach augmented views from input images.
- Sum instead of averaging cross entropy.
- Exponentiate unshifted logits.

## Actual CPU calibration

Eight deterministic asymmetric 4×4 glyphs generate 32 rotated examples. A zero-initialized 16×4 linear head learns for 80 full-batch SGD updates at learning rate `.6`. Both submitted functions are used. T3 requires rotation accuracy 1 and loss below `.06` and 5% of its initial value. Symmetric images cannot always reveal their rotation; the synthetic glyphs are chosen to make this pretext task learnable. Rotation accuracy alone is not evidence of transfer representation quality.

All data and initial parameters are deterministic; the test fixture also seeds Python/NumPy/PyTorch to 42. Native calibration uses the repository's PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU environment on Apple silicon. Tests use the same full training loop in the NumPy autograd adapter and exported WASM bundle. The gates validate numerical behavior and learning on this synthetic task, not a published paper benchmark.

Source: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07728) and [official implementation](https://github.com/gidariss/FeatureLearningRotNet/blob/master/dataloader.py).

Observed native reference metrics: initial_loss=1.38629; final_loss=0.0371615; initial_accuracy=0.25; final_accuracy=1.

Rotation affects only spatial axes. Every batch member and channel must survive, including when batch, channel and spatial dimensions are strided views. A scalar coordinate oracle checks the resulting views and parent-storage gradients.

provenance.adaptation: Original eight asymmetric 4x4 glyphs and their 32 exact rotations; 64 linear-head parameters, 80 full-batch SGD updates at lr .6, deterministic data and zero initialization. These are pretext training metrics, not transfer performance.
